implementation.improvement: Extended submit_many() zero-copy direct submission to the final partial chunk when flush_after=1 and no buffered entries exist. The synchronous batch ioctl receives the caller's validated array pointer directly instead of copying the final partial chunk into the internal retry buffer.
implementation.condition: The direct path is selected only when the batcher has no pending entries and the chunk either fills max_batch or is the final input chunk under flush_after=1.
implementation.partial_safety: Non-final partial chunks, partial completions, ioctl failures, and any path with pending buffered entries continue to use the internal retry buffer and remain retryable.
implementation.bounds: Direct chunks remain limited to the configured 1..64 kernel batch size. submit_many() retains its 4096-entry input bound and validates every entry before submission.
implementation.security: The change only selects a userspace pointer for a synchronous ioctl. Kernel authorization, lineage, tenant isolation, overflow checks, telemetry-loss handling, admission checks, and model-output-is-not-authority boundaries remain authoritative.

productivity_interpretation.benefit: A final three-entry flush chunk reaches the batch ioctl through the original caller array, avoiding one userspace copy in the no-pending synchronous path while preserving accepted-entry accounting and retry safety. The integrated gate also retains M161's two-to-one ioctl reduction for the full coalesced workload.
productivity_interpretation.scope: This proves pointer-path and submission-control behavior in a controlled unit test and QEMU integration environment, not end-to-end latency or memory-bandwidth improvement on physical accelerators.
productivity_interpretation.raw_throughput_scope: The integrated gate retained the inherited M155 synthetic QEMU accounting benchmark at speedup_x100=120 in this run; M163 does not claim an isolated raw-throughput gain.

build_artifact.kernel_source: M156 kernel image reused; M163 is userspace runtime/test/gate integration.

release_gate.reason: M163 is bounded userspace/QEMU validation. Physical accelerator qualification, independent reproducible production builders, signed artifacts, stable/LTS forward-port qualification, and external security governance remain required.
release_gate.hardware_claim: No physical GPU, NPU, VRAM, IOMMU, DMA, vendor-driver, reset, or fleet qualification is claimed.

known_limitations: Direct pointer use is safe only for the duration of the synchronous ioctl; this API does not support asynchronous retention by the kernel.
The measured copy avoidance is a controlled three-entry final-partial unit path, not a hardware memory-bandwidth benchmark.
The unit test uses an injected ioctl model; QEMU validates integration and packaging, not physical accelerator behavior.
No isolated M163 raw-throughput improvement is claimed; the M155 benchmark remains supporting context only.
The kernel remains based on the Linux v7.2-rc7 development line and production release qualification remains incomplete.
